adductor_magnus.name: Adductor magnus
adductor_magnus.plain: The largest inner-thigh muscle, running from your pelvis down the inside and back of your thigh.
adductor_magnus.why_it_matters: It helps drive you up from squats and hinges while keeping your hips strong and steady.

adductors.name: Inner thighs
adductors.plain: A group of muscles along your inner thighs that pull your legs inward and steady your hips.

heads.name: Adductor magnus
heads.plain: The largest member, helping pull your thigh inward and drive your hip backward.

heads.name: Other adductors
heads.plain: The smaller inner-thigh muscles that guide your leg and keep your pelvis controlled.

adductors.why_it_matters: Strong adductors improve squat control, hip stability, and the overall shape of your upper legs.

anterior_deltoid.name: Front delt
anterior_deltoid.plain: The front slice of your shoulder cap that raises your arm forward and helps with pressing.
anterior_deltoid.why_it_matters: Strong front delts support every chest and overhead press and add shape to the front of your shoulders.

biceps_brachii.name: Biceps
biceps_brachii.plain: The muscle on the front of your upper arm that bends your elbow and turns your palm up.

heads.name: Long head
heads.plain: The outer head that forms the 'peak' you see when you flex.

heads.name: Short head
heads.plain: The inner head that adds width to the front of the arm.

biceps_brachii.why_it_matters: The biceps build the peak of the arm — your number-one priority muscle for the look you want.

biceps_brachii_long_head.name: Biceps — long head
biceps_brachii_long_head.plain: The outer part of your biceps that runs over the shoulder and forms the peak when you flex.
biceps_brachii_long_head.why_it_matters: Building this head gives your upper arm a taller, sharper peak from the side.

biceps_brachii_short_head.name: Biceps — short head
biceps_brachii_short_head.plain: The inner part of your biceps that sits closer to your chest and helps bend your elbow.
biceps_brachii_short_head.why_it_matters: Building this head adds width and fullness to the front of your upper arm.

brachialis.name: Brachialis
brachialis.plain: A strong elbow-bending muscle hidden underneath your biceps on the front of your upper arm.
brachialis.why_it_matters: Growing it pushes your biceps upward and makes your arm look wider from the front and side.

brachioradialis.name: Upper forearm
brachioradialis.plain: The thick muscle running from your outer upper arm to the thumb side of your forearm.
brachioradialis.why_it_matters: It strengthens curls and gives your forearm a solid, muscular ridge near the elbow.

calves.name: Calves
calves.plain: The muscles on the back of your lower leg that lift your heel and help push you off the ground.

heads.name: Gastrocnemius
heads.plain: The visible upper calf with two rounded heads; it works hardest when your knee is fairly straight.

heads.name: Soleus
heads.plain: The broad muscle underneath; it works hardest when your knee is bent.

calves.why_it_matters: Strong calves support your ankles, power each step, and keep your lower legs in proportion.

core_stabilizers.name: Core stabilizers
core_stabilizers.plain: The deep muscles around your waist, spine, and pelvis that hold your trunk steady while your limbs move.
core_stabilizers.why_it_matters: A stable core lets you lift harder without your lower back or pelvis drifting out of position.

deltoids.name: Shoulders
deltoids.plain: The three-part muscle wrapping over your shoulder joint like a rounded cap.

heads.name: Front delt
heads.plain: The front slice that raises your arm forward and helps with pressing.

heads.name: Side delt
heads.plain: The outer cap that raises your arm sideways and makes your shoulders look broad.

heads.name: Rear delt
heads.plain: The back slice that pulls your upper arm backward and balances your shoulder.

deltoids.why_it_matters: Balanced delts build rounded shoulders and help your arms move strongly in every direction.

erector_spinae.name: Spinal erectors
erector_spinae.plain: Two long columns of muscle beside your spine that keep your back upright and help it extend.
erector_spinae.why_it_matters: Strong spinal erectors help you hold a safe, solid torso during squats, rows, and hinges.

forearm_flexors.name: Forearm flexors
forearm_flexors.plain: The muscles along the palm side of your forearm that curl your wrist and help close your hand.
forearm_flexors.why_it_matters: They build forearm thickness and help you keep a firm grip on weights.

gastrocnemius.name: Upper calf
gastrocnemius.plain: The visible two-headed muscle on the back of your lower leg that works across your ankle and knee.
gastrocnemius.why_it_matters: It creates the rounded calf shape and works hardest in calf raises done with a straighter knee.

gluteus_maximus.name: Glutes
gluteus_maximus.plain: The large muscle forming most of your butt that drives your hip backward and powers you upright.
gluteus_maximus.why_it_matters: Strong glutes power squats, hinges, running, and climbing while supporting a stable pelvis.

gluteus_medius.name: Side glute
gluteus_medius.plain: The fan-shaped muscle on the outer side of your hip that moves your leg outward and steadies your pelvis.
gluteus_medius.why_it_matters: It keeps your hips and knees from collapsing inward during walking, running, and single-leg lifts.

hamstrings.name: Hamstrings
hamstrings.plain: Three muscles down the back of your thigh that bend your knee and help drive your hip backward.

heads.name: Biceps femoris
heads.plain: The outer hamstring that helps bend your knee and gives the back of your thigh width.

heads.name: Semitendinosus
heads.plain: A long inner hamstring that helps bend your knee and extend your hip.

heads.name: Semimembranosus
heads.plain: A broad inner hamstring underneath that supports the same knee-bending and hip-driving jobs.

hamstrings.why_it_matters: Strong hamstrings balance your quads, power hinges, and help protect your knees.

hip_flexors.name: Hip flexors
hip_flexors.plain: A group of muscles at the front of your hip that lift your thigh toward your torso.

heads.name: Iliopsoas
heads.plain: The deepest and strongest hip flexor, running from your lower spine and pelvis to your upper thigh.

heads.name: Supporting hip flexors
heads.plain: Smaller helpers across the front of your hip and thigh that assist with raising your leg.

hip_flexors.why_it_matters: Strong, controlled hip flexors help you walk, climb, squat deeply, and keep your pelvis steady.

iliopsoas.name: Deep hip flexor
iliopsoas.plain: A deep muscle running from your lower spine and pelvis to your upper thigh that lifts your knee.
iliopsoas.why_it_matters: It helps you climb, run, and control your legs without your lower back taking over.

infraspinatus.name: Infraspinatus
infraspinatus.plain: A rotator-cuff muscle covering the back of your shoulder blade that turns your upper arm outward.
infraspinatus.why_it_matters: It keeps the shoulder joint centered and balanced during rows, presses, and overhead work.

lateral_deltoid.name: Side delt
lateral_deltoid.plain: The middle of your three shoulder muscles — the cap on the very top-outside of your shoulder.
lateral_deltoid.why_it_matters: Wide side delts are the single biggest trick for looking athletic: they broaden your frame and make your waist look smaller.

latissimus_dorsi.name: Lats
latissimus_dorsi.plain: The big fan-shaped muscle spreading from your spine to your upper arm — the widest muscle in your back.
latissimus_dorsi.why_it_matters: Wide lats are what make your shoulders look broad and your waist look smaller — the core of the V-taper.

latissimus_dorsi_lower.name: Lower lats
latissimus_dorsi_lower.plain: The lower fibers of your lats, sweeping from your low back toward your upper arm.
latissimus_dorsi_lower.why_it_matters: Building them extends the V-taper farther toward your waist and strengthens pulls toward your hip.

obliques.name: Obliques
obliques.plain: The muscles along both sides of your waist that rotate, bend, and brace your torso.
obliques.why_it_matters: Strong obliques give you a firm waist and keep your trunk steady when lifting or carrying.

pectoralis_major.name: Chest
pectoralis_major.plain: The big fan of muscle across the front of your ribcage that pushes your arms forward and together.

heads.name: Upper (clavicular) head
heads.plain: The top slice near your collarbone; incline pressing builds it and it's what reads as a 'full' chest in a shirt.

heads.name: Main (sternal) head
heads.plain: The larger lower-and-mid portion that flat pressing develops.

pectoralis_major.why_it_matters: A full chest — especially the upper part — is what makes you look built in and out of a shirt.

pectoralis_major_clavicular.name: Upper chest
pectoralis_major_clavicular.plain: The top slice of your chest near your collarbone that helps press your arm upward and inward.
pectoralis_major_clavicular.why_it_matters: Incline pressing builds this area, filling the space below your collarbones and making your chest look complete.

posterior_deltoid.name: Rear delt
posterior_deltoid.plain: The back slice of your shoulder cap that pulls your upper arm backward and outward.
posterior_deltoid.why_it_matters: Rear delts round out your shoulders from behind, support posture, and add width to your upper back.

quadriceps.name: Quads
quadriceps.plain: The four big muscles on the front of your thigh that straighten your knee.
quadriceps.why_it_matters: Strong quads drive nearly every lower-body lift and give your legs visible shape and overall body balance.

rectus_abdominis.name: Abs
rectus_abdominis.plain: The long muscle down the front of your stomach that curls your ribs toward your pelvis.
rectus_abdominis.why_it_matters: It forms the visible six-pack and helps keep your ribs and pelvis controlled during lifts.

rhomboids.name: Rhomboids
rhomboids.plain: Small, strong muscles between your shoulder blades that pull the blades back toward your spine.
rhomboids.why_it_matters: They thicken your mid-back and help you hold strong shoulder-blade position during rows and presses.

rotator_cuff.name: Rotator cuff
rotator_cuff.plain: Four small muscles wrapped around your shoulder joint that guide and hold the upper-arm bone in place.

heads.name: Supraspinatus
heads.plain: The top cuff muscle that starts lifting your arm and helps hold the joint centered.

heads.name: Infraspinatus
heads.plain: The broad back cuff muscle that turns your upper arm outward.

heads.name: Teres minor
heads.plain: A small back cuff muscle that assists outward rotation and shoulder control.

heads.name: Subscapularis
heads.plain: The front cuff muscle under your shoulder blade that turns your upper arm inward.

rotator_cuff.why_it_matters: A strong rotator cuff keeps pressing and pulling smooth while lowering the chance of shoulder irritation.

shoulder_stabilizers.name: Shoulder stabilizers
shoulder_stabilizers.plain: The smaller muscles around your shoulder blade and joint that keep everything lined up while your arm moves.
shoulder_stabilizers.why_it_matters: They give you a steady base for safe, strong pressing, pulling, and overhead lifting.

soleus.name: Deep calf
soleus.plain: The broad calf muscle underneath the gastrocnemius that lifts your heel, especially when your knee is bent.
soleus.why_it_matters: It builds lower-calf thickness and supports your ankles during walking, running, and seated calf raises.

teres_minor.name: Teres minor
teres_minor.plain: A small rotator-cuff muscle behind your shoulder that turns your upper arm outward.
teres_minor.why_it_matters: It helps keep your shoulder centered and controlled during pulling and overhead movements.

thoracic_spine_rotators.name: Upper-back rotators
thoracic_spine_rotators.plain: Small muscles around the middle and upper spine that help turn and steady your ribcage.
thoracic_spine_rotators.why_it_matters: They let your upper back rotate cleanly while your lower back stays controlled.

transversus_abdominis.name: Deep abs
transversus_abdominis.plain: The deepest abdominal muscle, wrapping around your waist like a built-in weight belt.
transversus_abdominis.why_it_matters: It braces your middle, supports your spine, and helps keep your waist firm during heavy lifts.

trapezius.name: Traps
trapezius.plain: The large diamond-shaped muscle from your neck across your upper back that moves and steadies your shoulder blades.

heads.name: Upper traps
heads.plain: The slope from your neck to your shoulders that lifts your shoulder blades.

heads.name: Middle traps
heads.plain: The fibers across your mid-back that pull your shoulder blades together.

heads.name: Lower traps
heads.plain: The lower fibers that pull your shoulder blades down and help them rotate upward.

trapezius.why_it_matters: Balanced traps support your neck and shoulders while adding thickness and control across your upper back.

trapezius_middle_lower.name: Mid and lower traps
trapezius_middle_lower.plain: The middle and lower fibers of your traps that pull your shoulder blades back, down, and smoothly upward.
trapezius_middle_lower.why_it_matters: They improve shoulder control, posture, and the dense upper-back shape behind your V-taper.

triceps_brachii.name: Triceps
triceps_brachii.plain: The muscle on the back of your upper arm — it's actually two-thirds of your arm's size, more than the biceps.

heads.name: Long head
heads.plain: The big inner slab; it crosses the shoulder, so it only fully works with your arm overhead.

heads.name: Lateral head
heads.plain: The outer 'horseshoe' you see from the side; pushdowns hammer this one.

heads.name: Medial head
heads.plain: A deep helper underneath that pitches in on every press.

triceps_brachii.why_it_matters: Bigger triceps make the whole arm look thick from the back and the side, not just the front.

triceps_brachii_long_head.name: Triceps — long head
triceps_brachii_long_head.plain: The biggest of the three triceps heads, running from your shoulder blade to your elbow.
triceps_brachii_long_head.why_it_matters: Because it crosses the shoulder, overhead moves stretch it fully — and a stretched muscle grows faster, building arm thickness.

whole_body.name: Whole body
whole_body.plain: A whole-body movement trains several major muscle groups together instead of isolating one small area.
whole_body.why_it_matters: It builds useful strength, coordination, and conditioning while getting more work done in less time.
